title: Musk Publicly Calls Out Altman, Says SpaceX Will Never Sell Computing Power to OpenAI

content_html:
The AI industry's compute arena recently saw a high-level war of words. According to media reports, as SpaceX continues to invest heavily in the data center sector, it is gradually growing into the most promising compute leasing provider in the United States. However, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk recently stated publicly on social media that SpaceX is not expected to sell any compute to its competitor OpenAI, and he set future sales to OpenAI at zero.

A Clash from Afar: The Collision Between the "Overstated Demand" Theory and Product Skepticism

The spark for this war of words came from earlier public remarks by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Altman once pointed out that current chipmakers clearly overestimate the compute demand of OpenAI and other large-model companies, and that "double counting" of orders is common in the industry. He believes that as multiple chip suppliers emerge in the market, outsiders often ask OpenAI about its demand and use that to infer the final market size, but in reality, leading companies including OpenAI will not buy every product from every chipmaker, and overall demand is somewhat limited and uncertain. Anthropic CEO Amodei also expressed a similar view earlier, saying that compute demand is difficult to predict accurately.

In response to Altman's "overstated demand" theory, Musk hit back bluntly. In a post on X, he said bluntly that if OpenAI's compute demand cannot grow rapidly, that precisely means the company's products themselves have a problem. Musk firmly believes that overall demand on the AI application side remains very strong, and he does not accept the so-called market bubble theory at all.

Expanding the Compute Map: Colossus Data Center Sprints Ahead

On the compute supply side, Musk is leading his team to continue ramping up infrastructure construction. As the core support for SpaceX's compute layout, its Colossus data center project is advancing its expansion at full speed.
